entities.name: Apollodorus of Seleucia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Apollodorus of Seleucia, or Apollodorus Ephillus, was a prominent Stoic philosopher and a pupil of Diogenes of Babylon, active in the Hellenistic era of the ancient world.

Born in the Seleucid Empire, Apollodorus of Seleucia's philosophical contributions were largely influenced by the teachings of his mentor, Diogenes of Babylon, who was in turn a student of the famous Cynic philosopher Antipater of Tarsus.

Apollodorus of Seleucia's philosophical ideas were shaped by the intellectual and cultural landscape of the Hellenistic world, where the intersection of Greek philosophy, science, and politics was forging new paths for human understanding.

Despite the passing of centuries, Apollodorus of Seleucia's works have left an enduring legacy in the annals of Western philosophy, where his ideas continue to be studied and debated by scholars today.

"The natural world is governed by reason and necessity," Apollodorus of Seleucia once wrote, echoing the fundamental principles of Stoic philosophy.
